claims.claim: Eaton Corporation plc identity and NYSE:ETN tradability are validated; reviewed primary operating evidence is Eaton's July 31 2026 Q2 release/SEC exhibit, corroborated by current independent market data for valuation.
Duplicate prior lineage around the same Eaton Q2 release is one issuer origin, not multiple independent confirmations.

provenance.freshness: operating primary dated 2026-07-31; market valuation observed 2026-09-21
provenance.duplicateOriginCollapse: Issuer release and SEC exhibit describe the same Q2 event and are not counted as independent corroboration.
provenance.sourceIndependence: Independent current market source is separate from issuer operating evidence.
provenance.rawVsDerived: Numeric operating claims trace to primary release/SEC exhibit; valuation assessment traces to independent current market data.

unknowns.unknown: Exact data-center share of backlog remains undisclosed in reviewed primary evidence.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 sales were $8.5B, up 21% year over year with 14% organic growth; operating cash flow was $1.1B and free cash flow $874M, up 23% and 22%.
Electrical Americas rolling orders rose 41% organically and backlog rose 33%; Electrical Global rolling orders rose 33% and backlog rose 103%.
Segment margin was 23.1%, down 80 bps year over year, creating a real mix/integration caution despite growth.
Current valuation is demanding: approximately $169B market cap, ~43x trailing P/E and ~28x forward P/E on 2026-09-21 independent market data.

thesisQuality.basis: Record sales plus 33%-103% electrical backlog growth support durable demand and value capture, but exact data-center backlog mix is undisclosed.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: 21% sales growth, 14% organic growth and 22%-23% FCF/OCF growth are strong, tempered by 80 bps year-over-year segment-margin contraction.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: ~43x trailing and ~28x forward P/E with ~$169B market cap is demanding relative to the calibration's downside-adjusted headroom test despite strong growth.

catalystScore.basis: Raised 2026 organic-growth guidance and the announced Mobility separation provide identifiable operating/portfolio catalysts, though execution timing remains material.

governancePower.basis: Management raised guidance after record results and is actively focusing the portfolio via Mobility separation; reviewed evidence supports disciplined execution but is insufficient for an exceptional stewardship score.

alignment2036.basis: Electrical distribution, protection and power-management capability is directly exposed to durable electrification, data-center and infrastructure load growth across end markets.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Electrical Americas, Electrical Global and Aerospace provide multiple demand engines; issuer states data centers are key while robust demand spans end markets.

bottleneckControl.basis: Large electrical backlog/order growth supports participation in constrained power-infrastructure capacity, but evidence does not establish Eaton as an irreplaceable sole bottleneck.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Demand is distributed across electrical and aerospace markets and is not solely dependent on AI/data centers, improving robustness across plausible infrastructure scenarios.

substitutionResilience.basis: Broad power-management portfolio and installed-channel exposure support replacement friction, while vendor/product substitution remains plausible and prevents an exceptional score.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Strong realized growth demonstrates current execution capacity, but reviewed evidence does not establish exceptional multi-source redundancy; unknown supply concentration is treated conservatively.

pricingPower.basis: Strong orders/backlog and 23.1% segment margin support commercial strength, but year-over-year margin contraction argues against assuming unrestricted price pass-through.

riskEvidence.basis: Principal risks are demanding valuation, 80 bps segment-margin contraction, acquisition/portfolio integration and normalization of elevated electrical demand/backlog.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Core operating claims are primary-source addressed and current valuation is independently sourced; confidence is reduced for undisclosed data-center backlog mix, supply concentration and limited proxy-specific governance evidence.

scoreRecord.thesis: Eaton is a high-quality power-management beneficiary of multi-year electrification and data-center infrastructure demand, with unusually strong order/backlog visibility and cash generation, offset by a demanding valuation and execution/mix risk.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: The market price already discounts substantial durable growth while segment margins have contracted year over year, leaving downside if backlog growth or integration economics normalize.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Conversion of elevated electrical backlog into sales/cash flow and execution of the announced Mobility separation, with the next earnings update expected in early November 2026.

risks.risk: Segment margin contracted 80 bps year over year despite strong growth.
Acquisition and Mobility-separation execution can dilute returns.

contradictions.claimA: Strong sales/order/backlog growth supports operating leverage.
contradictions.claimB: Segment margin was down 80 bps year over year.
contradictions.disposition: Resolved as a non-gating mix/integration caution and reflected in momentum, pricing-power and risk scores.

unknowns.unknown: Exact data-center share of backlog is undisclosed.
Reviewed evidence does not establish exceptional supplier redundancy or concentration.
